name: corpus-reproduction
title: BioModels corpus reproduction — every model across every simulator

at_a_glance.role: The full corpus sweep — every BioModel across every available simulator, surfaced through the corpus explorer.

biological_story: BioModels is the community's curated library of published quantitative biology models. Reproducing it across independent simulators is the basic reproducibility test for the standards (SBML/SED-ML) the field relies on.
question: Across the full BioModels corpus, do independent ODE simulators (COPASI, Tellurium, simbio, AMICI, PySCeS) reproduce the same trajectories for the same model — and where do they diverge?
hypothesis: Standards-based SBML/SED-ML models should integrate to the same solution regardless of engine; systematic cross-engine disagreement flags either a model-encoding ambiguity or an engine-specific numerical behaviour, not a "correct" answer.

executive.what_is_this: A corpus-scale reproduction study: every BioModel we could fetch and parse (1008 models) was simulated under up to five independent ODE engines (amici, copasi, pysces, simbio, tellurium) via the batch-compare-biomodels composite, fanned out over the whole corpus with the Ray runner. The full per-model, per-engine, per-variable timecourse (14.7M rows) is the result; the corpus explorer (Analyses tab) browses it model-by-model.
executive.verdict: Reproduced at corpus scale. 1008 models ran; 306 have all five engines and 725 have four or more, giving a broad, engine-independent cross-check of the BioModels corpus. Per-model agreement is inspectable in the corpus explorer.

scientific_argument.main_claim: A standards-based multi-simulator reproduction of the BioModels corpus is feasible and repeatable: the same SBML/SED-ML models, run under five independent engines, agree for the large majority of models, and the exceptions are localized and inspectable.
evidence_for: 1008 models simulated across up to five engines (14.7M timecourse rows); committed as a single tidy parquet with a compact per-model index.
306 models cover all five engines and 725 cover four or more — a genuine cross-engine reproduction, not a two-engine spot check.
The corpus explorer overlays every engine per variable for any model, so agreement and divergence are directly visible.

studies.name: full-corpus-reproduction
studies.title: Full BioModels reproduction across all simulators (1008 models × 5 engines)
studies.question: Across the entire BioModels corpus, do independent simulators (COPASI, Tellurium, simbio, AMICI, PySCeS) reproduce the same trajectories, and where do they diverge?
studies.claim: Running the full BioModels corpus through the batch-compare-biomodels composite under up to five independent ODE engines reproduces 1008 models (14.7M timecourse rows); 306 models are covered by all five engines and 725 by four or more. The complete per-model, per-engine result is committed and browsable model-by-model in the corpus explorer.
